question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between distance, time and speed when a body is NOT accelerating?
solution:
The correct answer is __**time=(distance)/(speed)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Speed** is defined as the distance traveled per unit of time. It is a scalar quantity.
 
• **Time** can be calculated by dividing the distance traveled by the speed if the speed is constant.
 
• The formula **time = distance/speed** is used when a body is traveling at a constant speed, implying no acceleration.
 
• This relationship is derived from the basic definition of speed: **speed = distance/time**.
 
• Understanding this relationship is crucial in various fields such as physics, engineering, and everyday problem-solving.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed**

 
 
• Measured in units of distance divided by time, such as meters per second (m/s) or kilometers per hour (km/h).
 
• It is a scalar quantity, meaning it only has magnitude and no direction.
 
 
 
• **Distance**
 
 
• Distance is a scalar quantity representing the interval between two points.
 
• It is measured in units such as meters (m), kilometers (km), etc.
 
 
 
• **Time**
 
 
• Time is a continuous, measurable quantity in which events occur in a sequence from the past through the present to the future.
 
• Measured in units such as seconds (s), minutes (min), hours (h), etc.
 
 
 
• **Constant Speed**
 
 
• When a body travels equal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be moving with a constant speed.
 
• This implies no acceleration or deceleration in the body's motion.
